doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: Debbie Allen and 'Pepito's Story' for the Kennedy Center
summary: He recalls working with Debbie Allen on a ballet and a musical, learning to write for dance.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Thank you for that. Wow, this has been delightful. Before we go I wanted to ask you a question sort of about back to your composing but when you do film scoring, do you get a scene — let me start with this. You did a commission, “Pepito’s Story” for the Kennedy Center Ballet.

Oh no, I’ve been collaborating and working with Debbie Allen in a lot of different events. That was the “Pepito’s Story” probably I think it was one of the first things I did with Debbie Allen which is an extremely talented artist. And I did a ballet, I did a musical with her, I did, oh my goodness, so many different things you know. And Debbie, you know, helped me to understand the process of writing for dance and writing for this and for this, different that. Because she is very smart you know. And I really appreciate it. I’m still collaborating with her you know. It’s a supreme lesson for me.
